S: › informal a state of being very tired in a nervous or slightly anxious (= worried and nervous) way after a lot of mental or physical effort
› UK informal a state of being completely burned or tired out

example: She's worn herself to a frazzle (= made herself very tired and nervous) trying to meet the deadline.
為了能如期完成，她把自己弄得筋疲力盡。
I went to answer the phone and when I came back the eggs were burned to a frazzle.
我去接了電話，回來的時候蛋都焦了。

NONE: › informal extremely tired in a nervous or slightly worried way after a lot of mental or physical effort
精疲力盡的，疲憊不堪的
› UK informal burned or dried out after being in the sun or cooking for too long
燒焦的；烤乾的

example: It was a stressful day at work and by 5.00 I was completely frazzled.
我今天工作非常緊張，五點鐘的時候就精疲力盡了。
I'd only been in the sun a couple of hours and my back was frazzled.
我才在太陽下兩個小時，後背就快曬焦了。
By the time I remembered about the meat it was frazzled.
等我想起來的時候，肉已經烤焦了。
